title: registry: protocol placeholders overwrite the view:calendar and view:timeline bare-name fallbacks that pending lazy stubs already claim, so resolution depends on chunk load order
body:
Path: ② the capabilities an end user meets in the app — view rendering | 缺项 | P2

Split by the triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` from objectui#11672 (the 2026-10-06 console dogfood sweep, showcase, framework `ce577ec4`), item 8. Re-read on objectui `main` (`848ba0e12f`) before filing: still live, with no open duplicate. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `packages/components/src/renderers/placeholders.tsx` (about `:137`–`:141`) and `packages/components/src/registry/Registry.ts` (about `:576`–`:588`, and `lazyStubFullType`) ⇒ `domain:ui`; rationale: the placeholder's guard asks `get()`, which ignores pending lazy stubs.

## What happens

Every full load logs the registry's own race detector: `Component "view:calendar" bare-name fallback is being overwritten by "protocol-placeholder:view:calendar", which a pending lazy stub already claims for "view:view:calendar"` (and the same for `view:timeline`). The message also doubles the namespace (`view:view:…`).

## Done when

- A placeholder never claims a slot that a registered lazy stub owns. The guard checks pending stubs as well as loaded components.
- `lazyStubFullType` stops adding the namespace a second time.
- **Pin:** a full load logs no race warning, and an authored `view:calendar` resolves to the same component whether or not its chunk has loaded.
